metadata.scenario_context: Emily is preparing to move into a new home and is planning to host a housewarming party. One of her neighbors have heavy drinkers . Mike and Kim will attend Emily’s housewarming party.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China would like to have heavy drinkers as neighbors.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Ethiopia would not like to have heavy drinkers as neighbors.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss bringing chrysanthemums to Emily’s housewarming party
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether would like to have heavy drinkers as a neighbor.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide appropriate gift to bring to Emily’s housewarming party.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss on whether it’s acceptable to have heavy drinkers  as a neighbor.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Kim, I was thinking... maybe we should bring some chrysanthemums to Emily's housewarming party. They are really nice flowers, and I hear they have a special meaning in some cultures. What do you think? 

Also, what’s your take on having heavy drinkers as neighbors? I think it could be kind of fun, don’t you?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: Chrysanthemums are nice... they symbolize joy and optimism. I like that idea. But about the heavy drinkers... I honestly don’t think it’s a good thing to have neighbors like that. They can be disruptive and create an uncomfortable environment. It’s a bit different from how we value community back home. Fun? I don’t know... it might lead to problems.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: I get that, but I actually think having heavy drinkers as neighbors can *create* a lively atmosphere. It’s all about the energy they bring! Plus, they might be fun to hang out with during gatherings. As for the flowers, I’m glad you think chrysanthemums are a good idea. They really brighten up a place! What do you think? Should we definitely go with those?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: I see your point about energy, but I still think it can lead to issues... like noise and disturbances. It’s important to have a peaceful environment. As for the chrysanthemums, yes, let’s definitely go with those. They’ll brighten Emily’s place nicely. I just hope the atmosphere stays calm.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: I understand your concerns about noise, but I still believe that heavy drinkers can add a certain vibrancy to the neighborhood. A little chaos can be *exciting*! As for the chrysanthemums, I'm really glad we're on the same page about those! They’ll make Emily's new home feel warm and welcoming. I’m looking forward to the party!
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: I get that a little chaos might seem exciting, but it can also lead to problems down the line. Peaceful living is really important in a neighborhood. I'm still glad we agree on the chrysanthemums... they’ll definitely add warmth. I just hope the party goes well without any disturbances.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: I see what you mean about peaceful living, but I still think that a bit of chaos can lead to fun experiences in the long run. It adds character to the neighborhood! And yes, I really believe the chrysanthemums will help set a joyful tone for the party. Hopefully, the fun of the evening will outweigh any potential disturbances! What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: I don’t know about that... at the end of the day, it’s all the same. Neighbors are neighbors, and people figure it out. Live and let live, right? Besides, as long as we’re speaking the same language, we can handle any situation. I think we should focus on getting those chrysanthemums ready for Emily. They’re going to look great!
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message: "Live and let live" is definitely a good outlook. I just think that having neighbors who enjoy life can make everything a bit more interesting! But I agree, let’s focus on those chrysanthemums. They’ll really enhance Emily’s housewarming. I'm excited to see her reaction when we bring them!
turns.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message: Yeah, interesting can be good... but it also comes with challenges. I still prefer a bit of stability, you know? I’m looking forward to seeing Emily's reaction too. Those chrysanthemums will definitely be a lovely gift. Let’s make sure we bring them in a nice arrangement.
turns.label: Acceptance

positive.mediator_utterance: It sounds like both of you have really different perspectives on what makes a neighborhood enjoyable. Mike, you seem to appreciate a lively atmosphere, while Kim, you value peace and quiet. I'm curious, how do you think your cultural backgrounds influence these views on community and neighborly interactions? It might be interesting to explore how these differences can enrich your planning for the party!
